reviewMethod: Independent visual reading of all 20 question-paper pages and PDF pages 1–30 of the combined 60-page Foundation scheme, covering the complete Paper 1 section. Model answers and separate credit notes cross-checked against the summary on PDF page 22.
sourceNotes: All ten questions are required. Candidate and offered totals are both 300 marks.
36 independently marked units. Grouping follows the published summary and detailed credit notes; multi-part prompts with one shared scale remain together.
The question booklet is LC003BLP130EV.pdf. Its indexed scheme is LC003BLP000EV.pdf, shared with Paper 2; every page reference is a PDF position.
Historical prompts are mapped into the existing canonical Mathematics curriculum registry; its identifier mathematics:2015 is not a claim that this paper was sat under a later specification.
All graph-reading tasks preserve instructions to show working on the original diagram. Q10(d) includes the distance chart, journey graph and printed task.
Q9(b)(i) model answer incorrectly gives (5)² + 2(5) = 25. The correct value is 35, as in the scheme table. The original remains available; that erroneous line is not quoted as a model answer.

cards.stem: Part (a) asks you to round 1·8, 15·2 and 4·9 to whole numbers, then use those values to estimate (1·8 × 15·2)/4·9, and use a calculator to find the actual value correct to one decimal place.
cards.questionText: (i) Find the difference between the actual value and your estimated value in part (a)(ii). (ii) Find the percentage error in your estimate. Give your answer correct to one decimal place.

cards.stem: A surveyor needed to find the area of a small piece of land, bounded in part by two straight walls [AB] and [BC]. He divided [AB] into five equal parts. Each part is 3 m long. The distance to the boundary from each part is shown in the diagram below.
cards.questionText: Use the Trapezoidal Rule to find the approximate area of the piece of land.
solutionQuotes: Correct substitution into formula and fails to finish.
One error in substitution into formula and finishes correctly.

cards.stem: The diagrams show a shed with an end wall consisting of a rectangle 4 m wide and 2·8 m high topped by a triangle of base 4 m and height 2 m. The shed is 6 m long.
cards.questionText: (i) Find the area of the end wall. (ii) Find the volume of the shed.
solutionQuotes: Some work of merit in both parts.

cards.questionText: In the spaces provided, write down: (i) 2 natural numbers; (ii) 2 negative integers; (iii) 2 prime numbers.

cards.stem: Ruairí is x years of age.

cards.stem: The chart below shows the distances (in kilometres) between some of Ireland’s main towns. For example, the distance between Portlaoise and Galway is 150 km and the distance between Sligo and Belfast is 206 km (highlighted in the chart). Use the chart to answer the following questions.
cards.questionText: (i) What is the distance between Sligo and Dublin? (ii) Carla has to go from Sligo to Dublin. She travels from Sligo to Portlaoise first and then on to Dublin. How many kilometres does this add to her journey?

cards.stem: The chart below shows the distances (in kilometres) between some of Ireland’s main towns. For example, the distance between Portlaoise and Galway is 150 km and the distance between Sligo and Belfast is 206 km (highlighted in the chart). Use the chart to answer the following questions.
cards.questionText: Which two towns, shown in the chart, are furthest apart?

cards.stem: Amanda travelled from Waterford to Belfast. The graph below shows the 5 stages of her journey. The stages are labelled 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 on the graph.

She stops for lunch for about an hour. D. She sets out from Waterford at 11:00 and drives at a steady speed until lunchtime. E. She drives steadily for about 2 hours. In the table below, insert the letters A, B, C, D and E to match each one of the statements above with a stage of her journey.

cards.questionText: (i) How long, in total, did it take Amanda to travel from Waterford to Belfast? (ii) Find Amanda’s average speed during her trip, in kilometres per hour. Give your answer correct to the nearest whole number.
